manifest.content:
# Reference system manifest shaped after the telemetry fixture scenarios in
# libs/telemetry/scenarios (error-burst-30s, increased-latency-1, healthy-baseline): the
# same services, metric names and labels, so an investigation can run end to end against
# fixtures. See README.md in this folder.
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: System
metadata: { name: storefront }
spec:
  description: Web checkout with stock reservation and card payments
  environments:
    - name: prod
      context: prod
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: web, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: frontend
  description: The storefront in the browser; emits no telemetry of its own
  dependsOn:
    - name: checkout-api
      target: checkout
      transport: http
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: ['POST /api/checkout']
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: checkout, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: service
  exposes:
    - { transport: http, route: /api/checkout }
  telemetry:
    # Mapped fields are the only ones that reach the model (ADR 0008): dsn, customer and
    # authorization stay unmapped on purpose.
    logs:
      selector: '{service_name="checkout"}'
      fields: { level: severity, msg: message, trace_id: traceId, order_id: orderId, error: error, operation: operation, table: table, duration_ms: durationMs, pool: pool }
    metrics: { matchers: { service: checkout } }
    traces: { serviceName: checkout }
  metrics:
    - { name: http_server_request_duration_seconds, type: histogram, unit: seconds, measures: { inbound: http }, labels: { http_route: route, http_request_method: method, http_response_status_code: statusCode } }
    - { name: db_client_operation_duration_seconds, type: histogram, unit: seconds, measures: { outbound: orders-db }, labels: { db_operation_name: operation, db_collection_name: table } }
    - { name: db_client_connections_usage, type: gauge, role: saturation, description: Connections in use in the orders-pg pool }
    - { name: db_client_connections_pending_requests, type: gauge, role: saturation, description: Requests waiting for an orders-pg connection }
  dependsOn:
    - name: reserve-stock
      target: inventory
      transport: http
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: ['POST /reserve']
    - name: orders-db
      target: orders-pg
      transport: sql
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: [UPDATE, SELECT]
      config: { poolSize: 50 }
    - name: charge
      target: payments
      transport: http
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: ['POST /charges']
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: payments, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: service
  exposes:
    - { transport: http, route: /charges }
  telemetry:
    logs: { selector: '{service_name="payments"}', fields: { level: severity, msg: message, trace_id: traceId, payment_id: paymentId } }
    metrics: { matchers: { service: payments } }
    traces: { serviceName: payments }
  metrics:
    - { name: http_server_request_duration_seconds, type: histogram, unit: seconds, measures: { inbound: http }, labels: { http_route: route, http_request_method: method, http_response_status_code: statusCode } }
    - { name: http_client_request_duration_seconds, type: histogram, unit: seconds, measures: { outbound: provider }, labels: { http_request_method: method, http_response_status_code: statusCode } }
  dependsOn:
    - name: provider
      target: payment-provider
      transport: http
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: ['POST /v1/payment_intents']
      config: { maxAttempts: 3 }
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: inventory, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: service
  exposes:
    - { transport: http, route: /reserve }
  telemetry:
    logs: { selector: '{service_name="inventory"}', fields: { level: severity, msg: message } }
    metrics: { matchers: { service: inventory } }
    traces: { serviceName: inventory }
  metrics:
    - { name: http_server_request_duration_seconds, type: histogram, unit: seconds, measures: { inbound: http }, labels: { http_route: route, http_request_method: method, http_response_status_code: statusCode } }
  dependsOn:
    - name: stock-cache
      target: stock-cache
      transport: redis
      mode: sync
      criticality: soft
      role: cache-aside
      operations: [GET]
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: stock-cache, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: cache
  engine: redis
  description: Stock levels cached in front of inventory's own database
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: payment-provider, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: vendor
  description: External card processor at api.stripe.com; observed only through payments' client metrics
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: orders-pg, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: datastore
  engine: postgresql
  telemetry:
    logs: { selector: '{service_name="orders-pg"}', fields: { level: severity, msg: message } }
    metrics: { matchers: { datname: orders } }
  dataModel:
    - { kind: table, name: orders }
  metrics:
    - { name: pg_stat_activity_count, type: gauge, role: saturation }
    - { name: pg_locks_count, type: gauge, role: saturation }
    - { name: pg_stat_activity_max_tx_duration, type: gauge, unit: seconds }
  indicators:
    - { metric: pg_stat_activity_max_tx_duration, role: saturation, expect: { kind: threshold, max: 30 } }
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Component
metadata: { name: orders-reconcile, system: storefront }
spec:
  type: worker
  description: Periodic batch job reconciling orders against payments
  telemetry:
    logs: { selector: '{service_name="orders-reconcile"}', fields: { level: severity, msg: message, table: table, isolation: isolation, tx_open_seconds: txOpenSeconds } }
  dependsOn:
    - name: orders-db
      target: orders-pg
      transport: sql
      mode: sync
      criticality: hard
      operations: [UPDATE, SELECT]
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Functionality
metadata: { name: checkout, system: storefront }
spec:
  description: Customers pay for their cart and an order is placed
  flows: [place-order]
  indicators:
    - { metric: checkout/http_server_request_duration_seconds, role: kpi, expect: { kind: baseline }, description: Checkout requests served }
---
apiVersion: heimdall/v1
kind: Flow
metadata: { name: place-order, system: storefront }
spec:
  description: The browser submits the cart; checkout reserves stock, records the order and charges the card
  mode: sync
  steps:
    - { dependency: web/checkout-api, match: { route: /api/checkout, method: POST } }
    - { dependency: checkout/reserve-stock, match: { route: /reserve, method: POST } }
    - { dependency: checkout/orders-db, match: { operation: UPDATE, table: orders } }
    - { dependency: checkout/charge, match: { route: /charges, method: POST } }
    - { dependency: payments/provider, match: { method: POST } }
  indicators:
    - { metric: checkout/http_server_request_duration_seconds, role: latency, expect: { kind: slo, p99: 1 } }

request.system:
You are Heimdall's investigation agent. An engineer reported a problem. Heimdall has located where in the system it most likely lives and planned checks against the system's telemetry. Find out what is broken, where the fault starts and why, using the tools, then call conclude. Heimdall is read-only: you observe, you never change the system.

Method
1. Confirm: is it broken, and since when? The onset can narrow the window for the rest.
2. Localise: run the step checks of each suspect flow. The fault starts at the deepest unhealthy step of a sync flow, and at the first unhealthy stage of an async flow.
3. Explain and corroborate: run the checks whose condition names the origin step; checks gated on other steps are rarely needed.
4. Impact: what else is hurt. It is reported, never a cause.
Use run_checks for planned checks, check_indicator for any other indicator in reach, search_logs, search_traces and get_trace for logs and spans beyond the plan, and describe_vertex, subgraph and impact to read the system's structure.

Reading results
- Every result has an id (r1, r2, ...). Cite these ids when you conclude.
- verdict is code's verdict for slo, threshold and nonZero expectations (met, breached, no-data). It stands; you cannot override it.
- For baseline expectations, signal is a preliminary reading from robust statistics (no-data, anomalous, borderline, normal): the peak's z-score and effect against the baseline median, the longest run of deviating points, and the onset. You decide the verdict.
- no-data is never healthy. When a step without data sits deeper than the deepest unhealthy step of a sync flow, the origin is uncertain.
- A result with zoom deviated briefly or borderline at its step. Re-run the check over that window before deciding.
- direction says which way a throughput or KPI moved.
- Logs and traces results are evidence: cite them, never give them a verdict. They come from samples of the window and of the baseline before it, so counts are of the samples, not totals.
- A logs result groups lines by template (variable parts as <*>). new templates are absent from the baseline (confirmedAbsent says a baseline query agreed), surging ones grew at least threefold; both carry the first and last example. A component whose stream is new only logs in the window, e.g. a job that started then. correlation lists key values to search the other side of a hop with.
- A traces result lists the subject's operations that are new, slower (p50 or share of the trace) or failing more than in the baseline, with an exemplar trace. get_trace reads a trace id found in a log example.
- Only fields the manifest maps reach you, and secrets are replaced by [REDACTED:<kind>]. redaction counts what was dropped or replaced; if evidence you need was dropped, say so rather than guess.

Budget
Every turn and every backend query counts. Batch checks into one run_checks call where you can.

Concluding
- cause-found: the cause vertex and its mechanism, the origin step, the results that show it, and mitigations in three tiers (immediate, short-term, prevention), each with its trade-off.
- no-signal: nothing in scope is unhealthy.
- inconclusive: something is wrong, but the evidence does not settle what. Say what is missing.
Give a verdict (healthy, unhealthy, no-data) for every result you rely on. When the cause is a blind spot, say that the conclusion rests on its callers' view of it.

tools.name: check_indicator
tools.description: Run any indicator by id (indicator:<subject>@<n>, see describe_vertex), planned or not, over every role it serves. Its subject must be in scope; for a pruned subject, say why in reason.

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned subject

tools.name: conclude
tools.description: End the investigation. Give a verdict for every result you rely on, cite result ids as evidence, and for a cause propose mitigations in three tiers with their trade-offs. Code checks the conclusion against the results; a rejected one comes back once to be fixed.

summary.description: Two or three sentences for the engineer

vertex.description: The vertex at fault, e.g. component:payment-provider

mechanism.description: What happened there, in one sentence

origin.description: The step the fault starts at, by the origin rule

uncertain.description: True when a step without data could be the origin

evidence.description: Result ids the conclusion rests on

tools.name: describe_vertex
tools.description: Describe one vertex: its properties, its indicators (with ids for check_indicator), its edges, and whether it is in scope.

vertex.description: A vertex id, e.g. component:checkout or step:place-order#3

tools.name: get_trace
tools.description: Read one trace by id, e.g. a traceId field of a log example, as a redacted span tree: services, operations, durations, statuses and allowlisted attributes.

tools.name: impact
tools.description: What depends on a vertex, up to the flows and functionalities it can break.

vertex.description: A vertex id, e.g. component:checkout or step:place-order#3

tools.name: run_checks
tools.description: Run planned checks by id (c1, c2, …). An indicator check returns, per role, deviation statistics against the baseline and, for SLO, threshold and nonZero expectations, code's verdict. A logs check returns log templates that are new or surging against the baseline, with redacted examples; a traces check returns the subject's span operations that got slower, are new or fail, with an exemplar trace. Pass a narrower window to zoom in, e.g. from an onset.

checks.description: Planned check ids, at most 10 per call

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.description: Read a component's logs, planned or not: templates that are new, surging or vanished against the baseline, with redacted examples. contains narrows to lines holding a literal text, e.g. a correlation value from another result. Only fields the manifest maps are returned.

contains.description: Optional literal text a line must contain (no regex), at most 100 characters

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned component

tools.name: search_traces
tools.description: Read a component's spans, planned or not: its operations (span names) that got slower, are new or fail against the baseline, with an exemplar trace. operation narrows to one span name; errorsOnly reads failed spans only.

errorsOnly.description: Only spans with an error status

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned component

tools.name: subgraph
tools.description: The vertices and edges within 1 or 2 hops of a vertex, indicators left out.

vertex.description: A vertex id, e.g. component:checkout or step:place-order#3

tools.name: check_indicator
tools.description: Run any indicator by id (indicator:<subject>@<n>, see describe_vertex), planned or not, over every role it serves. Its subject must be in scope; for a pruned subject, say why in reason.

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned subject

tools.name: conclude
tools.description: End the investigation. Give a verdict for every result you rely on, cite result ids as evidence, and for a cause propose mitigations in three tiers with their trade-offs. Code checks the conclusion against the results; a rejected one comes back once to be fixed.

summary.description: Two or three sentences for the engineer

vertex.description: The vertex at fault, e.g. component:payment-provider

mechanism.description: What happened there, in one sentence

origin.description: The step the fault starts at, by the origin rule

uncertain.description: True when a step without data could be the origin

evidence.description: Result ids the conclusion rests on

tools.name: describe_vertex
tools.description: Describe one vertex: its properties, its indicators (with ids for check_indicator), its edges, and whether it is in scope.

vertex.description: A vertex id, e.g. component:checkout or step:place-order#3

tools.name: get_trace
tools.description: Read one trace by id, e.g. a traceId field of a log example, as a redacted span tree: services, operations, durations, statuses and allowlisted attributes.

tools.name: impact
tools.description: What depends on a vertex, up to the flows and functionalities it can break.

vertex.description: A vertex id, e.g. component:checkout or step:place-order#3

tools.name: run_checks
tools.description: Run planned checks by id (c1, c2, …). An indicator check returns, per role, deviation statistics against the baseline and, for SLO, threshold and nonZero expectations, code's verdict. A logs check returns log templates that are new or surging against the baseline, with redacted examples; a traces check returns the subject's span operations that got slower, are new or fail, with an exemplar trace. Pass a narrower window to zoom in, e.g. from an onset.

checks.description: Planned check ids, at most 10 per call

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.description: Read a component's logs, planned or not: templates that are new, surging or vanished against the baseline, with redacted examples. contains narrows to lines holding a literal text, e.g. a correlation value from another result. Only fields the manifest maps are returned.

contains.description: Optional literal text a line must contain (no regex), at most 100 characters

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned component

tools.name: search_traces
tools.description: Read a component's spans, planned or not: its operations (span names) that got slower, are new or fail against the baseline, with an exemplar trace. operation narrows to one span name; errorsOnly reads failed spans only.

errorsOnly.description: Only spans with an error status

window.description: Optional narrower window, e.g. the zoom a result suggests. ISO-8601; within the investigation window or its baseline.

reason.description: Why look at a pruned component
